about: Milestone 3 conventions and plan for Hawiyah 0.3.0, written at commit a0ed9b0. File and line references were read in this step unless marked as taken from triage.

conventions.rule: When adapters differ, the choice is made in this order and recorded with its basis. (1) Guidance recorded in this repository decides: CONTRACT.md, components.json, docs/*.md (docs/dga-checklist-review.md for Platforms Code checklist rows, the docs/nic-*.md measurement records, docs/readonly-inputs.md, docs/multiselect-validation.md, docs/tag-input-interaction.md) and the authored vanilla markup those documents show. The documented vanilla markup is the reference DOM: element names, hw- classes, data- attributes and child order; the three frameworks render that DOM. (2) If the repository is silent, the behaviour with the better accessibility result wins (a name for every control and landmark, focus never lost, state exposed to assistive technology, announcements not duplicated). (3) Only then the majority of adapters; on a tie the smaller public change. A majority never overrides (1) or (2). Recording: every specification carries a `decisions` list of {component, question, choice, basis: 'repository' | 'accessibility' | 'majority', source: file:line or the reason, changedAdapters}. The implementer copies each entry into CHANGELOG.md under Unreleased (Breaking when a public name, default or rendered DOM changes) and, where a docs/<component>.md record exists, adds one line there; CONTRACT.md is edited only for rules that hold across components. A recorded decision that is reversed (for example docs/input-review.md:29-32 on reset) is rewritten in place, not left beside the new rule.

perAdapter.react: Changes follow the decision; no behaviour is kept 'because React does it'.
perAdapter.angular: Same. Angular is not the reference merely because the guide is written in it.
perAdapter.vanilla: Authored markup in docs and components.json is the reference DOM; a controller never rewrites authored names (CONTRACT.md:69-77).

conventions.rule: 0.3.0 is a breaking release: a rename or removal is made outright in every adapter in the same commit, with no deprecated alias, no second selector kept for compatibility and no runtime shim. Triage remainders that say 'alias for one release' (nav-b-2, nav-b-17, E06, R26, service-patterns-1, choices-5) are overridden by this rule. Every specification lists its renames in `renames`: {adapter, component, kind: 'input' | 'output' | 'field' | 'selector' | 'default' | 'markup' | 'removed', from, to, migration} where migration is one line a reader can apply by search and replace, written as before -> after. The implementer adds them to CHANGELOG.md Unreleased under a heading 'Breaking: renamed and removed' as a table (adapter, component, from, to, migration), updates components.json, llms.txt, the package READMEs and docs/ in the same change, and tests/text-contract-docs.test.ts must still pass. A changed default or changed rendered DOM is listed the same way with kind 'default' or 'markup'. The renames this document already fixes are in the top-level `renames` list; a specifier may add to it but may not choose a different target name for a meaning listed there.

conventions.rule: A native reset is a value change made by the form. One microtask after a `reset` event that was not default-prevented, every Hawiyah control (a) holds its reset target, (b) shows it, (c) submits it in FormData, and (d) has reported it once through its ordinary value notification if and only if its value changed (arrays and tuples compared by content). After the microtask the three of (a)-(c) always agree, also when the application controls the value and ignores the notification: then the control shows and submits the application's value again. Reset target: React and Vue: `defaultValue` (or the matching default prop), else the component's documented empty value ('' , [], false, null, the slider midpoint). Angular: when Angular Forms is attached (registerOnChange was called) Angular Forms owns the value and the component changes nothing by itself (FormGroupDirective and NgForm already write null on a native reset, which the component maps to its empty value); otherwise the target is the value the component held after its first ngOnInit. Vanilla: the values authored in the markup, captured when the controller is created. Read-only does not exempt a control (docs/readonly-inputs.md:13, docs/combobox-readonly.md:29); a read-only control that was never changed therefore keeps its value. A disabled control is reset too. Secondary state returns to its initial state in the same microtask without a notification of its own unless it changed: popups close, the query and any draft are cleared, PasswordField returns to hidden, file lists are emptied, DatePicker restores draft and month, custom validity is recomputed and aria-invalid set by a failed submission is cleared. One shared listener: core `observeFormReset(control, onReset): {destroy()}` (new, packages/core/src/form-reset.ts) resolves `control.form` (so the `form` attribute is honoured), listens for `reset`, waits one microtask, skips when default-prevented or destroyed. This reverses docs/input-review.md:29-32 and docs/nic-segmented.md:27 for Angular (owner decision 1).

perAdapter.react: Composite components (everything with `onValueChange`): `useFormReset(ref, reset, form)` (react/src/expanded-shared.ts:3) calls a reset that goes through `useControllable`'s setter, so uncontrolled state moves to `defaultValue ?? empty` and `onValueChange(target)` fires only when the value differs; ToggleGroup's `if (value === undefined) setInternal(...)` (react/src/expanded-interactive.tsx:22) is replaced by that setter. Controlled (`value` given): `onValueChange(target)` fires when target differs from the prop; the component then bumps a reset counter in state so that the next render rewrites `checked`/`value`/hidden inputs from the prop the application renders (fixes actions-v1). Native pass-through controls (TextField, Textarea, Select, Checkbox, Radio, Switch: react/src/forms.tsx:16-60) keep React's own behaviour: uncontrolled returns to `defaultValue` with no `onChange`, controlled keeps the application's value; the only addition is that a controlled Select and controlled choices rewrite the DOM from the prop after the reset. This exception is documented in the React README.
perAdapter.vue: `useFormReset(element, reset)` (vue/src/shared.ts:35) stays the hook. `reset` calls `model.set(target)` only when target differs from `model.value.value`, otherwise `model.sync(target)`; `useValue.set` (vue/src/shared.ts:28-34) gains that comparison once so every control gets it. `update:modelValue(target)` is therefore emitted once per changed control and never for an unchanged one (fixes actions-11); a multiple ToggleGroup's empty value is [] (vue/src/expansion-interactive.ts:27-30). Select without `defaultValue` resets to the option the browser selects after the reset, read from the element (vue/src/forms.ts:58-61, fixes fields-basic-9). With `modelValue` bound and the update ignored, the next tick rewrites the DOM from `modelValue`.
perAdapter.angular: `HwValueControl` (angular/src/forms.ts:17-40) owns the mechanism for every value control, including those extending `HwExpandedValueControl` (angular/src/advanced-controls.ts:13-19): fields `private formsBound = false` (set in registerOnChange), `private initial!: T` (set in ngOnInit, after the first inputs), and, in the browser only (afterNextRender), `observeFormReset(firstFormControlOf(host) ?? host, () => this.resetFromForm())`. `resetFromForm()`: if (!formsBound) { const target = this.initial; if (!sameValue(this.value, target)) { this.value = target; this.valueChange.emit(target); } } then `this.afterReset()` (protected hook: close popups, clear query/draft/files, revealed = false) then `this.syncDom()` then `markForCheck()`. `syncDom()` is a protected method each component implements to write the held value to its native controls as properties (`checked`, `value`, `selected`, hidden inputs); the text field uses `InputValueSync.force()` (angular/src/input-value.ts:11). It bypasses the `disabled` guard of `update()` (forms.ts:38). No `defaultValue` input is added in Angular. The private reset listeners in hw-password-field (advanced-controls.ts:37-38) and hw-search-field (:101-102) move into `afterReset()`.
perAdapter.vanilla: Each controller captures `initial` at creation and already listens with the same microtask pattern (vanilla/src/controls.ts:30,69,108,131,191,237,289; content.ts:57,87; combobox.ts:185-187; calendar.ts:176,274). They switch to core `observeFormReset` and, new, call `emit(root, {value})` and `options.onValueChange` when the reset changed the value. Native inputs inside the root are reset by the browser; the controller re-renders derived DOM (pressed buttons, chips, slots, outputs).

conventions.rule: An Angular component is one of two kinds, chosen in this order. (A) Host is the root: when the root needs no particular native element (div, span, section with a role), the host element carries the hw- class and state attributes through `host: {class: 'hw-x', ...}` and the template is the content only; class, id, style, aria-* and data-* that the application writes on the element are then on the element the stylesheet styles, with nothing to forward. When the root must be a native element that an application can write itself (a, button, nav, article, table), the component is an attribute selector on that element (`button[hwButton]` at presentation.ts:11, `nav[hwSideNavigation]` at side-navigation.ts:11) and the element selector is kept only if it can also be a valid root. (B) Host is a wrapper: when the root must be a native element inside a structure the component renders (input, select, textarea inside a field; fieldset; dialog; progress; meter; details) the host stays a wrapper and exactly these attributes are forwarded as inputs under their attribute names: `@Input({alias: 'aria-label'}) ariaLabel: string | null = null`, `@Input({alias: 'aria-labelledby'}) ariaLabelledby: string | null = null`, `@Input({alias: 'aria-describedby'}) ariaDescribedby: string | null = null`, and on form controls `@Input({alias: 'aria-invalid', transform: booleanAttribute}) ariaInvalid = false`; the component adds `host: {'[attr.aria-label]': 'null', '[attr.aria-labelledby]': 'null', '[attr.aria-describedby]': 'null', '[attr.aria-invalid]': 'null'}` (shared constant `forwardedAriaHost` in new packages/angular/src/host-attributes.ts) so the attribute never stays on the role-less wrapper, and binds the values on the element that needs them. The application writes `aria-label="..."` or `[aria-label]="expr"`; `[attr.aria-label]` on a wrapper host is not supported and is documented as such. The existing `describedBy` input is renamed to this `aria-describedby` input (owner decision 2). Nothing else is forwarded from a wrapper: `id` stays on the host and the inner control keeps `controlId` (tooltip: `tooltipId`), so no id is ever duplicated; `class` and `style` stay on the host, which is a block box through the zero-specificity list in styles/src/layout.css:133 (add each wrapper there instead of component `styles`); every documented data-variant / data-size / data-tone value is an input (`variant`, `size`, `tone`) that the component writes on the root, and an authored data- attribute of the same name is not a second way to set it. Rule for a kind-A host that also writes an attribute the application may write (aria-label from `label`, role): never a host binding, which would remove the application's value; use the mechanism of HwSectionComponent (layouts.ts:53-70), moved to `HwHostAttribute` in host-attributes.ts: written in ngDoCheck only while the component has a value, the application's value put back otherwise. Default assignment for the open items (a specifier may deviate only with a recorded reason): kind A host-root: hw-badge, hw-chip, hw-spinner, hw-skeleton, hw-avatar, hw-avatar-group, hw-button-group, hw-empty-state, hw-alert, hw-stat, hw-cookie-consent, hw-side-navigation (already); kind A attribute selector: `a[hwLink]` replaces the hw-link component (removed), `button[hwButton], a[hwButton]` stay; kind B wrapper with forwarded ARIA: every HwValueControl, hw-toggle-group, hw-radio group, hw-progress, hw-meter, hw-card, hw-table, hw-data-table, hw-dialog, hw-drawer, hw-popover, hw-menu, hw-tree-view, hw-tabs, hw-breadcrumb, hw-pagination, hw-stepper, hw-notification-list, hw-content-navigation, hw-feedback, hw-carousel, hw-accordion.

conventions.rule: Every control, group and landmark gets its accessible name from, in this order: an `aria-label` from the application, an `aria-labelledby` from the application, the surrounding Field label, the component's `label`. `label` is required only when none of the others is present, and a missing name is reported once through requireText under the component's own name; an optional `label` renders no empty label, legend or attribute. The rule is the same in the four adapters; only the declaration differs.

E05: TreeView and ContentNavigation switch from a plain required `label` to RootName + rootLabel; E02: ToggleGroup routes `label` through text() and omits the legend when it is missing; E03: `footerLabel` and `externalLabel` become unions on the prop that switches them on.
perAdapter.vue: `label` is declared without `required: true` and checked at render with `rootLabel(component, props.label, attrs)` (vue/src/shared.ts:58-62) or `useField` (shared.ts:14-26). E05: TreeView `label` becomes optional + rootLabel; E02: ToggleGroup uses needText and omits the legend.

HwValueControl binds on the native control: `[attr.aria-label]="ariaLabel"`, `[attr.aria-labelledby]="ariaLabelledby ?? (field ? field.labelId : null)"`, and renders its own `<label>` only when `label` is given (forms.ts:43 already does). Group roots (fieldset, role=group, nav, section, dialog) bind the same two attributes and fall back to `label`. This closes fields-basic-2, choices-3, E08 and R22 with one mechanism.

conventions.rule: A required control with a visible label shows one marker: ` *` as the last child of its `label.hw-label` or `legend.hw-label`, in every adapter and for every control, including composite ones and fieldset groups. It is present exactly when the control is required (its own `required` or the one inherited from Field) and absent otherwise; it is never the only carrier of the requirement: the native control keeps `required`, a role=radiogroup group gets `aria-required="true"`, and a group that only has a custom constraint (MultiSelect, TagInput) explains it in its hint as docs/multiselect-validation.md:23 says. The glyph is not application text and gets no input. No other marker markup is allowed (React MultiSelect's bare span is replaced).

conventions.rule:
Order inside `.hw-field` (and inside a fieldset group after its options): label or legend, control, hint, error. Elements: `

` and `

` in every adapter (the documented vanilla markup; React changes from div, Vue from span); hint and error content is phrasing content. The control's aria-describedby lists, in this order, the application's ids, the Field's ids, the hint id, the error id, without duplicates. There is at most one `.hw-error` per control. Two sources fill it: the application's `error` (static text: no role, it is read with the control through aria-describedby), and a message the component itself produces after the reader acted (a constraint from a `...Message` input such as requiredMessage, invalidMessage, unsupportedMessage, unavailableMessage, or a file rejection from getRejectedMessage): that one is rendered in the same element with `role="alert"`, inserted only while it applies and removed when the value becomes valid or the form resets. Status that is not an error (results count, selected count, formatted date, copy feedback) is never in `.hw-error`: it is a `role="status"` element that exists, empty, from the first render (CONTRACT.md:183-185). conventions.rule: `aria-invalid="true"` is on the native control (on the fieldset for a group) exactly when one of these holds, and the attribute is absent otherwise: (1) the application passes a non-empty `error`; (2) the application passes an explicit aria-invalid (React and Vue: the attribute; Angular: the forwarded `aria-invalid` input); (3) a submission failed on this control: its `invalid` event fired (checkValidity, reportValidity or requestSubmit), and the state stays until the control's validity becomes valid after a value change, or the form resets; (4) the reader committed a non-empty value that violates a constraint the component checks itself (DatePicker: malformed, out of range, unsupported, unavailable; PinInput: wrong length once complete; FileDropzone: a rejected file). It is never set because a required control is still empty before any submission, and never because a message text is missing: Angular's `unnamedConstraint` (forms.ts:176, advanced-controls.ts:211) is removed. (3) applies to every Hawiyah control that sets a custom validity (Combobox, MultiSelect, TagInput, DatePicker, PinInput, ToggleGroup and Rating when required); plain native controls keep the browser's own invalid state and :user-invalid styling. The `invalid` event is not default-prevented.

conventions.rule: One pattern per adapter for every piece of state other than the value (`open`, `visible`, `expanded`, `query`, `index`, `page`, `month`, `calendar`, `sort`): the state has one name, the same in the four adapters, and three members derived from it. conventions.rule: Read-only means: the control keeps its place in the tab order, keeps its accessible name, keeps its named value in FormData, shows its value, and cannot be changed by pointer, keyboard, paste or drop; it is never rendered as `disabled` and never replaced by text. Exposure: native `readonly` on text inputs and textareas; `aria-readonly="true"` on roles that define it (combobox, slider, spinbutton, searchbox, the DatePicker text input); `aria-disabled="true"` on checkbox, radio, switch, toggle buttons and the file input, guarded by core `observeReadonlyChoice` (docs/readonly-inputs.md:8-10); a group root carries `data-hw-readonly="true"` for styling. Notifications never fire for a blocked change. Navigation that changes no value stays available (opening a read-only tree branch, moving focus, scrolling a list). Prop name: `readOnly` in React and Angular, `readonly` in Vue (Vue Checkbox, Radio and Switch rename `readOnly`), the native `readonly` attribute or `data-hw-readonly="true"` on the root in vanilla. conventions.rule: Where React accepts a ReactNode, the other adapters must accept rich content for the same part, by one mechanism each. (1) The single primary content of a component: React `children`, Vue default slot, Angular `<ng-content />`, vanilla authored children. conventions.rule: Type-ahead is one core helper used by Menu and TreeView in the four adapters (and by any later list with roving focus). New packages/core/src/typeahead.ts, exported from core index: `createTypeahead(options?: {timeout?: number}): {next(key: string, labels: readonly string[], current: number, isDisabled?: (index: number) => boolean): number; reset(): void}` and `isTypeaheadKey(event: {key: string; ctrlKey?: boolean; metaKey?: boolean; altKey?: boolean}): boolean`. Behaviour, taken from the two vanilla implementations: a key counts when it is one character, not a space, with no Ctrl, Meta or Alt; it is passed through core `normalizeSearch` and appended to a buffer that clears 500 ms after the last key; when every character of the buffer is the same the search uses that single character, so repeating a letter cycles; the search starts at the entry after `current`, wraps, skips disabled entries and returns the first whose normalised label starts with the buffer, or -1. The caller moves focus to the returned index and calls preventDefault only when an entry was found. `labels` are the visible texts in visual order: in a tree, the visible (expanded) nodes only. The helper holds no DOM reference, starts its timer only inside `next`, and so is safe to create during server rendering; adapters create one per component instance and call `reset()` when the list closes or unmounts.

conventions.rule: Keyboard focus is never dropped to the document body by a control's own activation. (a) A control that stays in the DOM but becomes unavailable because of the activation (Carousel and Pagination previous / next at a bound, a step button at the last step) is not given the `disabled` attribute for that reason: it gets `aria-disabled="true"`, stays focusable, keeps its accessible name, and ignores click, Enter and Space; the stylesheet already styles `.hw-button[aria-disabled='true']` like a disabled button. The `disabled` attribute remains for unavailability that the reader did not cause on that control (the whole component disabled, fewer than two slides, a disabled form). (b) A control that is removed by its own activation (tag remove, toast or alert dismiss, notification dismiss, file remove, chip remove) hands focus, in the same render, to the same control of the next item, else of the previous item, else to the component's primary control or its container made focusable with tabindex="-1" (TagInput: the text input; lists: the list root). Core `toast-focus.ts` is the model and is reused. (c) A popup that closes returns focus to its trigger only when focus was inside it (Popover Escape: nav-b-8); when focus leaves a non-modal popup it closes without moving focus (nav-b-7).

Cross-adapter cases live in tests/<component>-parity.test.ts in the existing form: one `mount(adapter, ...)` helper returning the same handles for all adapters and `for (const adapter of ['vanilla','react','vue','angular']) it(`${adapter}: [RESET-01] ...`)`; an adapter is left out of a case only with a comment that names the reason and the convention that allows it. Assertions are made on the DOM, FormData, document.activeElement and the recorded notifications, never on component internals, so one assertion body serves the four adapters. Adapter-only cases (types, hydration, Angular Forms) live in the package's own test files with the same id scheme. The Angular side of a parity test imports the built package (tests/toggle-group-parity.test.ts:5), so the Angular package is rebuilt before the parity run. A specification lists, per case id, the file it goes in. A fixed defect keeps a regression case whose title also carries the audit id, for example `[RESET-05][actions-v1]`. Browser-only facts (layout, computed style, focus rings, forced colours) go to tests/browser/*.spec.ts with the same ids and load only the package stylesheet in a static fixture.

conventions.rule: For every component a specification changes: (1) the server HTML equals the first client render, attribute for attribute; anything that depends on the browser (the owning form, validity, focus, the location, measurements, clipboard) is read only after mount: React in effects, Vue in onMounted, Angular in afterNextRender or behind injectIsBrowser, and core helpers are created lazily. (2) No module evaluates a browser global, and no listener (reset, invalid, focusout, pointerdown, keydown on document) is attached during server rendering. (3) Ids are deterministic: React useId, Vue useId, Angular injectId / HwIdSource; ids of hint and error derive from the control id. (4) State that only an interaction can produce starts in its initial value on both sides: aria-invalid from a failed submission is absent, popups are closed unless the application opens them, status elements exist and are empty, component-produced `.hw-error` is absent. (5) Controlled and default values render the same DOM on the server as after hydration, including `checked`, `selected`, `open` and hidden inputs. (6) Angular forwarded attributes: on the server the inner element carries the value and the host does not; hydration reuses that DOM without a mismatch; `HwHostAttribute` writes through Renderer2 and reads static values through HostAttributeToken so that it does not depend on the hydrated DOM. (7) Angular templates that hide empty projection regions with `:empty` emit no whitespace inside the region. (8) Vanilla modules import without a DOM and controllers are created only in the browser.

ownerDecisions.question: Reset: may a native form reset change a Hawiyah control's value and notify the application, in Angular (without Angular Forms) and for controlled React components? This reverses docs/input-review.md:29-32 and docs/nic-segmented.md:27.
ownerDecisions.why: Today a reset leaves Angular showing an empty control while the model and, for multi-select, the submitted hidden inputs keep the old value (triage actions-2, fields-basic-8, rich-inputs-5, dates-5, files-5). 'Model wins, reset does nothing' would be consistent but makes a reset button silently skip Hawiyah controls beside native ones.

ownerDecisions.question: Angular wrapper hosts: forward four attributes as inputs under their own names (aria-label, aria-labelledby, aria-describedby, aria-invalid), rename `describedBy` to `aria-describedby`, replace hw-link by a[hwLink], and state that [attr.aria-label] on a wrapper host is not supported?
ownerDecisions.why: The approved decision covers label and labelledby; an aria-describedby left on a role-less wrapper is the same silent defect. Input aliases work for static and bound values and under hydration. hw-link cannot carry routerLink or ARIA to its anchor.

ownerDecisions.question: choices-5: rename Angular hw-radio to hw-radio-group in 0.3.0 and leave the new group components for React, Vue and vanilla to 0.4?
ownerDecisions.why: The rename is the only breaking half and 0.3.0 is the breaking release; the new components are additive.

ownerDecisions.question: TagInput: remove Angular's Add button and its required addLabel, or add an opt-in Add button to all four adapters?
ownerDecisions.why: docs/tag-input-interaction.md:3 records that all four adapters commit with Enter or comma; three adapters have no button and the layouts then match.

ownerDecisions.question: TreeView expand and collapse (nav-b-13, R21): a named button inside the tree item in every adapter, or a decorative glyph everywhere?
ownerDecisions.recommendation: Named button (button.hw-tree-toggle, tabindex -1, getExpandLabel / getCollapseLabel), so Angular gains two required texts.
ownerDecisions.why: A touch screen-reader user cannot press ArrowRight; without a named control a branch cannot be opened when activating the item selects it. React and Vue already do this.

ownerDecisions.question: Popover and Collapsible text (nav-b-9, R26): `label` as the accessible name with no packaged heading, or `title` rendered as a visible heading?
ownerDecisions.recommendation: `label` in all adapters; React renames title to label and stops rendering the Popover heading; a visible heading goes in the content with aria-labelledby.
ownerDecisions.why: Vue and Angular already use label; small popovers often have no heading; the name rule (aria-label, aria-labelledby, label) then is the same as for every other root.

ownerDecisions.question: Menu and Popover trigger (R15, nav-b-3): keep the application's own element in React and a packaged button in Vue and Angular, with triggerVariant defaulting to 'secondary'?
ownerDecisions.recommendation: Keep both mechanisms for 0.3.0, add triggerVariant with default 'secondary' to Vue and Angular, defer trigger projection.
ownerDecisions.why: A disclosure trigger is rarely the primary action of a view; Angular's primary default is the outlier. Unifying the mechanism is additive and can wait.

ownerDecisions.question: Feedback and CookieConsent (service-patterns-12, R04, R05): adopt one contract based on React's? Feedback: value {helpful: boolean, comment: string}, a comment step and submit in all four, state `value`, action `feedback`. CookieConsent: state `open`, action `consent('accepted' | 'rejected')`, optional `preferences`, named by its h2.
ownerDecisions.recommendation: Yes; Angular gains commentLabel and submitLabel as required texts, Vue renames accept / reject to consent, React replaces value / CookieChoice by open + onConsent.
ownerDecisions.why: Three incompatible contracts cannot be documented as one component; this is the largest breaking change of the milestone and touches public events in three adapters, so it needs the owner's word.
